A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DEM-MOE study and three experiments. Their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations on five datasets, synthetic-annotation and data-blending experiments, and PCC annotation statistics.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds zero-shot comparisons, demographic coefficient tables and subgroup-level results.

M1.justification: The Bayesian embeddings, top-k expert routing, loss components, phased training, synthetic-data generation and blending procedures are retained. Expanded architectural explanations do not establish a procedural change.

E1.justification: Both versions use Offensiveness, Politeness, Safety, Toxicity and PCC with the same task coverage. New subgroup analyses reuse represented populations; newly described PCC recruitment targets do not establish changed sampling.

E2.justification: v2 adds zero-shot LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct to the Experiment 1 comparison through Appendix C.2 and Tables 20–24. v1 included its LoRA version in that comparison; its separate LLaMA-8B prompting pilot does not constitute the same comparison. Other comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: The added comparison evaluates text-only zero-shot LLaMA against demographic-prompted LoRA, and Appendix D.1 introduces finer subgroup aggregation of MAE by group frequency. Existing instance-level splits, annotator overlap, metrics and training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds a capacity-versus-inductive-bias diagnostic and a five-dataset analysis of synthetic-label errors across demographic subgroups and frequencies. It also expands demographic-regression reporting into full coefficient tables. Existing seen/unseen-annotator, expert-specialization and prompting analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Bootstrap error bars, significance markers and 95% confidence intervals already appear in v1. The additional interval-bearing tables extend uncertainty reporting without introducing a new statistical procedure, run count or seed-reporting practice.

E6.justification: v2 adds zero-shot comparison scores, extensive subgroup MAEs and fuller demographic-regression results. The reported PCC age coefficient changes from 2.38 in v1 Section 3 to 2.5280 in v2 Table 8. Existing headline scores in Figure 1 and Table 2 remain unchanged; the additions are not same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The routing equations, composite training loss, synthetic-example weighting and specialization mathematics are retained. Neither version adds a theorem or proof, and the new parameter-count discussion is empirical interpretation.

C1.justification: The abstract and three headline contributions remain stable. However, Section 2 narrows the novelty claim from no prior recommendation or NLP work jointly modeling individual and group preferences with MoEs to no prior NLP work doing so.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations attributing performance to inductive bias rather than capacity and suggesting underfitting on Safety. It interprets subgroup fidelity with specific exceptions and adds substantive limitations concerning Prolific sampling and annotation-question wording in Section 9.

D1.justification: v2 specifies the ModernBERT-large baseline's CLS regression head and mean-rating target, reports trainable parameter counts, and discloses PCC racial and gender recruitment targets. These are documentation additions; training hyperparameters, hardware, runtime information and access arrangements are retained.

R1.justification: The substantive discussion adds Gong et al. (2023), Shuai Liu et al. (2025) and Orlikowski et al. (2023), acknowledges recommendation-system precedents, and distinguishes intersectional modeling. The bibliography expands considerably, but the actual revision of research positioning is focused.

P1.justification: Substantial rewriting and compression affect the introduction, recommendation-related work, dataset descriptions, method motivation, baseline descriptions and synthetic-data motivation. New appendix subsections reorganize supporting material. Citation rendering also changes, including the malformed 'holland1987cultural' citation.

P2.justification: v2 adds demographic-coefficient, zero-shot-comparison and parameter-count tables, five subgroup-MAE figures, and a Max Coef column in Table 1. Figure 1 uses narrower, nonoverlapping bars, while existing heatmaps and other figures are relocated.

improvement.justification: The new subgroup results and baseline tables make the evidence more transparent, while explicit PCC sampling and wording limitations improve qualification of the findings. The gain is limited: the capacity argument remains indirect, and malformed citations and an expanded, partly duplicated bibliography weaken presentation. Overall, these additions modestly improve the paper without changing its central evidence.
